title: Layers and the build cache
summary: Why instruction order decides whether a rebuild takes two seconds or two minutes, and what .dockerignore is for.

steps.title: An image is a stack of layers
body: Each `RUN`, `COPY` and `ADD` produces a **layer**: the set of files it added or changed. An image is those layers stacked, and a container adds one writable layer on top.
│ FROM node:22-alpine 160 MB   │  ◀── shared by every image built on it

When you rebuild, Docker reuses (**caches**) a layer if the instruction is identical, its parent layer is cached, and, for `COPY`/`ADD`, the copied files have identical contents. The moment one step misses, **every step after it runs again**.
So: put what changes **rarely** (base, dependency install) near the top, and what changes **often** (your source) near the bottom.

steps.prompt: With this Dockerfile, you edit one line in `src/index.js` and rebuild. Which steps run again?
options: `COPY . .` and every step after it, so `npm ci` reinstalls everything
Nothing; Docker detects that package.json did not change
steps.explain: `COPY . .` copies the changed file, so it misses, and every following step (including the slow install) runs again. Copy `package*.json`, install, and only then copy the rest.

steps.prompt: Arrange a cache-friendly Dockerfile for a .NET API: restore packages from the project file alone, then copy the code and publish.
steps.explain: Editing `Program.cs` now re-runs only the last two steps; the NuGet restore stays cached until `Api.csproj` changes.

steps.title: .dockerignore
body: `docker build .` first sends the **build context** (the whole folder) to the builder. A `.dockerignore` file next to the Dockerfile excludes paths, with the same idea as `.gitignore`:
1. **Speed**: no shipping hundreds of MB of `node_modules` or `.git` to the builder.
2. **Cache**: without it, `COPY . .` sees changes in `bin/` or `.git` on every build and misses.
3. **Safety**: `.env` files, keys and local settings never end up inside an image someone can pull.
Your own `node_modules` or `bin/obj` from the host would also clash with what the image installs or builds for Linux.

steps.explain: The lock file must be in the context: `npm ci` needs it to install exactly the tested versions.

steps.prompt: Why do Dockerfiles write `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl` as **one** step, instead of two separate RUN lines?
options: As two steps, the cached `apt-get update` layer can be months old when a later edit adds a package, so the install uses stale package lists
Docker only allows one apt-get per Dockerfile
Two RUN steps would run in parallel and conflict
`&&` makes the commands run as root
steps.explain: Combining them means the index is always refreshed exactly when the package list changes. Adding `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` in the same step also keeps the index out of the layer.

steps.prompt: Install curl in a Debian-based image without leaving the package index in the layer.
steps.code: RUN apt-get update __1__ apt-get install -y __2__ curl __3__ rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
steps.explain: Files deleted in a *later* step still occupy space in the earlier layer. Clean up in the same RUN.

steps.prompt: You need a completely fresh build (for example to pick up a security fix behind an unchanged `apt-get` line). Which command ignores the cache?
steps.explain: `--pull` also helps: it checks the registry for a newer version of the base image instead of using the local copy.

steps.title: Fix the cache order
prompt: This terminal has a **real Docker Engine**. `~/shop` builds with a slow dependency install (it stands in for
`dotnet restore` or `npm ci`). Build it twice, changing one source line in between, and watch the install run again:
echo '# tweak' >> src/app.sh && docker build -t shop/app:dev .
Reorder the Dockerfile so that a change under `src/` **reuses the cached install**, while a change to `deps.txt` still
reinstalls. The image must keep working: `docker run --rm shop/app:dev` prints `app ready (3 packages)`.

checks.name: the image builds and runs
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && docker build -q -t shop/app:dev . >/dev/null && docker run --rm shop/app:dev
checks.fail: `docker build` fails or the app does not start.

checks.name: a source change keeps the install cached; a deps.txt change reinstalls
checks.fail: The check builds a copy of `~/shop`, changes `src/app.sh`, then `deps.txt`. Copy only what the install needs first, run it, then copy the rest.

hints: The cache breaks at the first instruction whose input changed, and everything after it rebuilds.
`COPY . .` copies `src/` too, so any source change invalidates the install that follows it.
Copy `deps.txt` and `install-deps.sh` first, `RUN` the install, and only then `COPY . .`.
solution: echo '# tweak' >> src/app.sh && docker build -t shop/app:dev .
steps.explain: Layer caching is a chain: an instruction is reused only when it and everything before it are unchanged. Copying the dependency manifest first means the expensive restore only reruns when the dependencies change, which is the difference between a 2-second and a 2-minute rebuild on every commit. Real .NET Dockerfiles do exactly this: `COPY *.csproj` and `dotnet restore` before `COPY . .`.
